title: Nonowantuck (Crystal Brook)
summary: Nonowantuck is connected with Mount Sinai in Brookhaven. The placename refers to a small stream that once ran from the interior plains toward the west side of Mount Sinai Harbor, leaving a valley later known as Crystal Brook.
history_content: This placename brings together the Mount Sinai location, the remembered Crystal Brook valley, and the dry-creek interpretation. It is a place-name and landscape note, with source details available through the reference icon system.
translation_content:
No separate spelling variants are listed in the available references. The name is interpreted as a creek that dries up or a dry creek, from a root connected with drying and the creek suffix -tuck.

Why Place Names Matter

“Some names carry the presence of ancestors, their journeys, their teachings, their conversations with the land. These names mark moments of connection, remembrance, and responsibility, kept alive through generations.”

— Native Land Digital, Indigenous Place Names (2024), The Story of Place is Alive section
whereintheworld_content: Approximate general point in the Crystal Brook area of Mount Sinai, near the west side of Mount Sinai Harbor. The map placement is for orientation only, not an exact stream course, valley boundary, or archaeological coordinate.
